describes_date: the army's own standing orders in the scene year
repository: National Library of Medicine, via the Internet Archive
locator: Recruiting Service arts. 19-21; Quarter Master's Department arts. 31, 82; Post and Company Funds arts. 27-30
rights_note: A United States government publication of 1835.
note: Read for T-1349, and it is the army's own book in the scene year. Three things are taken from it. Recruiting Service art. 19: 'All free white male persons, above the age of 18, and under 35 years, being at least 5 feet 6 inches high ... may be enlisted. This regulation, so far as it respects the height and age of the recruit, shall not extend to musicians, or to those soldiers who may re-enlist into the service' - which is the enlistment age band and its two exemptions, and also the Army's own colour bar, recorded as a fact about the institution. Quarter Master's Department art. 31: '225 square feet of room' to every six non-commissioned officers, musicians, privates and servants, 'including the authorized number of washerwomen, at posts above the 38th degree of north latitude' - Chicago is above it, and that allowance is an independent check on the garrison. And the laundress articles (27-30, 82), which quarter, pay and settle the accounts of a company's washerwomen while referring throughout to 'the authorized number' WITHOUT PRINTING IT; art. 82 is the only place a proportion appears, one washerwoman to every seventeen persons, and it is a straw allowance rather than an establishment.
